query: What causal mechanisms link social capital (informational, instrumental, aspirational ties) to higher education access among Chinese high school graduates?

response.query: What causal mechanisms link social capital (informational, instrumental, aspirational ties) to higher education access among Chinese high school graduates?
response.answer: Social capital enhances higher education access for Chinese high school graduates through informational, instrumental, and aspirational ties that provide guidance, resources, and motivation. These ties facilitate better academic preparation and application processes.

results.title: Linking social capital to green purchasing intentions in livestreaming sessions: the moderating role of perceived visible heterogeneity | Humanities and Social Sciences Communications
results.content: Despite the acknowledged importance of green purchasing for environmental sustainability, the mechanisms and conditions through which social capital impacts green purchasing behaviors in the context of live-streaming marketing are not well understood. A mixed-method approach employing Structural Equation Modeling and Necessary Condition Analysis investigates the pathways through which social influence and interaction shape social capital and subsequently influence green purchasing intentions. This analysis focuses on the mediating effect of customer inspiration (CI) and the moderating role of perceived visible heterogeneity (PVH), drawing on survey data from consumers participating in live-streaming sessions that promote green products. Moreover, shared green value, and green trust emerge as indispensable necessary conditions supporting green purchasing intention.
